content.thinking:
The io-shop account pages failed after deploy P2 of revision 696c33a. The metrics place the onset at 07:29, which is before the deploy at 07:30:24, so the deploy may not be the trigger.

I'm checking whether the 07:29 onset in the metrics really predates the 07:30:24 deploy, since that gap could mean the deploy isn't the trigger. The rollback restoring service is what ties the deploy to the failures, and the errors begin around 07:30. Next I'm looking at how the mixed old and new replicas read the summary cache entries.

I'm weighing whether the new writer's '2400/8' entries are what the old reader trips over, since the failing reads trace back to that format rather than to anything else in the repo. The scenario's cache fixture returns that exact string, and the log line shows it being rejected as not a figure in cents.

I'm checking whether the root cause holds up. The new revision writes cache entries as "2400/8", and the old revision's reader seems to reject that shape, which would fail the account pages while the rollout sits half-done. The log lines and the format change support this, though the old reader's parsing code isn't shown in the diff.

I'm settling on the cause: the change switched the summary cache entry to a two-field "2400/8" text, and the replicas still on the old revision, whose reader expects a bare cents figure, raise a ValueError on those entries. With the rollout paused at half, the old replicas kept hitting the new-shape entries, which is what failed the account pages.

I'm going back over how the cache entry is described, and I'll stick with a plain "two-field amount/items text" rather than quoting the value itself. I'm also questioning why the rollback fixed things, since rolling back would still leave the old replicas meeting the same entries. The likely answer is that the stand-in cache lookup is part of the deployed code, so rolling back reverts it along with the rest, and the rollback result already confirms that. I'm not going to speculate further about it.

I'm checking whether the deploy really is the trigger, since the metrics show onset at 07:29, a little before the 07:30:24 rollout. For the five-whys, I'm tracing the account page failures to the ValueError on the summary cache entries, which points back to the new two-field format, and I'm looking at the 361 minutes of metrics before onset to see whether the service was healthy under P1.

I'm ruling out the P1 deploy: the metrics show account pages rendering normally from 07:02 to 07:18 after it, and the rollback restored service with P1's revision still in place. Flag changes also look unlikely, since none were recorded in the window. I'm keeping the bad deployment as a live candidate, since it converged with the failures.

I'm settling on how to word the onset gap: the metrics put onset a minute before the deploy's recorded time, and the record doesn't explain that, so I'll note it as a loose end rather than treat it as settled.

I'm weighing the contributing factors now: the rollout was paused with mixed revisions running, but the real question is whether the change itself broke compatibility with the shared cache entries. That points to the entry shape changing without a versioned key or an old-side reader that tolerates it, rather than the pause being the cause.

I'm weighing the contributing factors: the change altered the shape of a shared cache entry without a versioned key, and nothing in the record shows a mixed-version compatibility test before it went out, so that gap is one I'll flag. The old reader raising on an unreadable entry, instead of treating it as a miss, is also a missing safeguard, though it doesn't change the root cause.

I'm drafting the contributing factors now, and I'm weighing whether a missing safeguard in the old reader belongs there. The old reader raising on an unreadable entry instead of treating it as a miss is a gap, but the fix for it already sits in the new code, so I'm leaning toward dropping it. I'm also considering whether nobody being paged is a factor worth recording, though it may not change the outcome.

I'm weighing whether a rollout-pause or missing auto-rollback on error rate belongs among the contributing factors, since the alert came after its rule waited. I'm leaning toward leaving that for the response section rather than the cause chain.

I'm checking whether the rollout's lack of an error-rate gate or automatic rollback is worth recording as a contributing factor, since the alert only fired after its rule waited. I'm also noting the ClientDisconnected errors that began before the onset, which look like background noise rather than part of the failure.

Still weighing what could follow from the fix: if the automatic sync gets turned back on before the repo is corrected, it would put revision 696c33a back and the failures would return. Redeploying that revision, or anything carrying its two-field cache entries, could break account pages again while replicas of the earlier revision are still serving. Next I'm turning to the action items, starting with the preventive ones.

Next I'm drafting the action items, covering a mixed-version compatibility test in CI, an expand-then-contract rule for shared cache formats, a rollout health gate that rolls back on error rate, and routing the HighErrorRate alert to on-call paging.

I'm noting that the Investigator pinned down the mixed rollout, Argus ruled out flag changes from the provider history, and the rollback restored service and was confirmed. The Code-Fix Agent kept none of its fix, since its benefit depended on code outside the repository. Nobody was paged during the incident, which is a finding to record on its own.

I'm noting the assumptions to state: the onset minute gap, and that the failing reader is the old revision's, inferred because the new reader returns None instead of raising, though the old reader's code isn't in view. I'm also leaving out the rollout-pause angle as a luck factor, since the new reader's graceful handling is by design.

I'm now phrasing the chain's first step: the shoppers' account page requests failed, with the failing share rising well above normal, and I'm citing the alert and the log entries for that without adding figures. The second step is that those requests raised a ValueError when reading the summary cache entry, which was in an amount/items text shape rather than a figure in cents. I'm about to tie that two-field shape back to revision 696c33a.

I'm checking the P1 ruling against the metrics, which read back over the hours before the onset and show the service at its usual error rate, with the confirmed rollback leaving it back to normal. Next I'm working on the fourth step of the chain: the mixed rollout meant that half the replicas still ran the earlier revision while the new entries were being written.

I'm drafting the root cause now: revision 696c33a changed the summary cache entry from a bare figure in cents to an "amount/items" text, and the copies still on the old revision could not read that shape. I'm keeping each timestamp tied to the row it was read from, so the state at 07:30 stays separate from the state I'm citing at the paused rollout.

I'm working out the contributing factors now: a mixed-version compatibility test on the shared cache format was never seen before the change shipped, and that gap would have caught the incompatibility before deploy. The rolling update's lack of a health gate that rolls back on error rate is the second one I'm recording.

I'm settling the third contributing factor now: the old revision's reader fails the page on an unreadable entry rather than treating it as a miss, so a fallback there would have let pages render, if more slowly. That belongs in the contributing factors, not the root cause, so I'm taking the "instead of falling back" wording out of the root cause.

I'm settling the last open question: the root cause should stop at the incompatibility, and the fallback point belongs as its own contributing factor. For that I'll add an action item requiring every summary cache reader to treat an unreadable entry as a miss, since the old revision can't be changed but the new one already does this.

action_items.item: Add a CI test that runs the previous revision's summary cache reader against entries written by the new revision, and the reverse, so a change to a shared entry shape cannot ship if a mixed rollout would break it.
Make it a review rule that any change to the shape of a shared cache entry either writes under a new versioned key or first ships a reader that accepts both shapes, before the writer changes.
Add a test that every summary cache reader treats an entry it cannot parse as a miss and falls back to working out the figure, never failing the page.
Add an error-rate health gate to io-shop rolling updates that halts the rollout and rolls it back automatically when the error rate rises above its baseline.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of the service's requests that failed rose well above its usual level.
Those requests failed because reading the shopper's summary cache entry in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py raised a ValueError: the entry was an 'amount/items' text, not a figure in cents.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 5470c1a (P1). The metrics read back over the hours after it show the service at its usual error rate until the onset, account pages logged as rendering normally after it, and the confirmed rollback left that revision running with the service back to normal.
A feature flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the investigation read it, and the flag read returned no flags.

causal_chain.step: Entries in that two-field shape came from revision 696c33a, deployed at {P2.1}. It changed a cache entry from a bare figure in cents to one text holding the figure and the number of purchases behind it.
The new shape broke pages because, as read at {T10.1}, the rolling update was paused with {T10.5} replicas still on revision 5470c1a, and those replicas could not read the two-field entries.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed the format the shop uses to save each shopper's spending summary, and the copies of the shop still running the previous version expected the old format, could not read the new entries, and failed the account page.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that tested the change against the previous revision reading the same cache, such as a mixed-version compatibility test, before a change to the shape of a shared cache entry went out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The old reader's failure on the new entry shape would have been found before the deploy, and the change would not have reached production in a form the running replicas could not read.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The previous revision's cache reader fails the account page when it meets an entry it cannot read, instead of treating the entry as a miss and working the figure out, which is what the module's own docstring says should happen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Replicas on the old revision would have skipped the new entries and rendered the page more slowly, and the format mismatch would not have failed requests.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No rollout health gate was seen that halts and rolls back an io-shop rolling update when errors rise. The rollout stayed in place, with both revisions serving, until Argus rolled it back.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The rolling update would have been reverted automatically once errors rose, ending the failures sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's rollout state and found the rolling update paused, with replicas on both revisions.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else, which ruled flags out.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the io-shop deployment for C1.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service after the rollback and judged the action confirmed once the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent kept none of the fix it wrote, once its reading showed the fix would help only together with a change outside the repository.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.

input.root_cause: Revision 696c33a changed what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare figure in cents to an 'amount/items' text, and wrote it where the previous revision also reads, with no versioned key or other way to keep the two shapes apart. Replicas still running revision 5470c1a share that cache during the paused rolling update, and their reader expects a bare cents figure, so it raised ValueError on the new entries and the account page request failed.
input.still_at_risk: Deploying revision 696c33a again, or any revision that writes the two-field cache entries, could make account pages fail again while replicas of the earlier revision are still serving.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
